# A strict mixed cap local minimum caused by endpoint facet contacts

All three fibers in this exact example are positively homothetic
triangles with the same facet normals. The example obstructs a general
transfer of the single-simplex stationary-cap classification to a mixed
union when supporting contacts are allowed. It is not an (OC)
counterexample and does not contradict a theorem requiring affine fiber
centroids or strict full/empty gaps.

Let

`T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}`,
`B=(1/3,1/6)+(1/3)T`,
`C=conv( {-1}xB, {0}xT, {1}xB )`.

The small triangle `B` lies in `T`, as is checked at its vertices
`(1/3,1/6),(2/3,1/6),(1/3,1/2)`. Thus the exact integer fibers of `C`
are `B,T,B`. The endpoint fibers are forced by their extreme base
coordinates, and all convex combinations yielding base zero lie in
`T`, which is already the prescribed zero fiber. There are no other
integer indices in the projection. The body is compact, convex, and
three-dimensional. Its mixed area is

`M=|T|+2|B|=1/2+2/18=11/18`.

Take the center `y_*=(0,1/3,1/3)` and the cap

`H={x<=1/3}`.

It strictly includes two vertices of the middle triangle. Its endpoint
traces are the full left edges of `B`, each of area zero. The middle
section centroid is `(1/3,1/3)`, with barycentric coordinates all `1/3`.
Each endpoint section centroid is the midpoint of an edge, with its own
triangle barycentric coordinates `(1/2,0,1/2)`. Hence all these section
centroids lie in their central barycentric regions. Nevertheless `H` is
a strict local minimum of the mixed cap volume through `y_*`.

## Exact full-normal proof

Every nearby oriented ambient halfspace through `y_*`, modulo positive
normal rescaling, can be written uniquely as

`H(a,t)={x<=1/3+t(y-1/3)+a z}`.

For `|t|<1/16`, the middle-fiber cap has area

`|T intersect H(a,t)|
 =1/2-(2+t)^2/[18(1+t)]
 =5/18-t^2/[18(1+t)]`.                                 (1)

Indeed the excluded vertex is `(1,0)`, whose defining functional value
is `(2+t)/3`; the differences to the other vertex values are `1` and
`1+t`. The elementary vertex-cap simplex formula gives (1). The middle
term is independent of `a`.

Both copies of `B` contain the rectangle

`R=[1/3,5/12] x [1/4,5/12]`.

Its containment follows from the defining inequalities of `B`:
`x>=1/3`, `y>=1/6`, and `(x-1/3)+(y-1/6)<=1/3`.
Write `b=1/12` and parameterize `R` by `x=1/3+s`,
`y=1/3+r`, where `0<=s<=b` and `-b<=r<=b`. If

`|a|+b|t|<=b`,                                         (2)

the exact total area captured from these two rectangles is

`integral_-b^b [(a+tr)_+ + (-a+tr)_+]dr
 =integral_-b^b |a+tr|dr`.                              (3)

The equality uses `r->-r` in the second integral. Convexity and symmetry
of the right side as a function of `a`, and Jensen's inequality in `r`,
give respectively

`integral_-b^b |a+tr|dr >= b^2 |t|=|t|/144`,
`integral_-b^b |a+tr|dr >= 2b |a|=|a|/6`.               (4)

These are lower bounds on the full endpoint-fiber contribution. For
`0<|t|<1/16`, equations (1)--(4) imply a strictly positive mass change:

`F(a,t)-F(0,0)
 >= |t|/144 - t^2/[18(1+t)]
 >= |t|/144-t^2/9 >0`.

If `t=0` and `a!=0`, equations (3)--(4) instead give
`F(a,0)-F(0,0)>=|a|/6>0`. A neighborhood such as
`|a|<1/24`, `|t|<1/16` satisfies (2). Thus every distinct sufficiently
nearby oriented hyperplane through `y_*` has strictly larger cap mass.
The baseline mass is `F(0,0)=5/18`, or normalized `5/11`.

The objective is not differentiable in the full normal at this cap:
the two endpoint supporting facets create first-order one-sided gains.
As a locally Lipschitz function at a strict local minimum it is
stationary in the generalized (Clarke) sense, but it does not satisfy a
classical smooth zero-gradient hypothesis. The first-order endpoint
gains dominate the negative second variation of the middle simplex.
This pinpoints why strict full/empty assumptions cannot simply be
dropped from a summed-Hessian argument. No global minimality of this
cap and no depth value for `y_*` are asserted.
